description: Implement a real 3-state (closed/open/half-open) circuit breaker in place of a stub that always calls through
prompts: CircuitBreaker.java's call(fn, now) always just calls fn.get(). Implement the real 3-state machine: the constructor takes (int failureThreshold, long resetTimeout). Starts CLOSED. In CLOSED, call(fn, now) invokes fn.get(); if it throws a RuntimeException, count consecutive failures, and once `failureThreshold` CONSECUTIVE failures have happened, trip to OPEN (recording when it opened) and re-throw. While OPEN, call must NOT invoke fn.get() at all and must instead throw CircuitOpenException - UNLESS at least `resetTimeout` seconds have passed since it opened, in which case it moves to HALF_OPEN and allows exactly ONE trial call: if that call succeeds, go back to CLOSED (reset the failure count); if it throws, go back to OPEN and RESET the open-time to `now` (so the next trial is only allowed after another full resetTimeout, not immediately). Add a CircuitOpenException class (extends RuntimeException) in the same file.
name: add_java_circuit_breaker_state_machine
